```{r packages}
have <- need %in% rownames(installed.packages())
if (any(!have)) install.packages(need[!have], repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
invisible(lapply(need, library, character.only = TRUE))

# A small helper for HC1 robust coefficient tests.
robust_test <- function(model) {
  lmtest::coeftest(model, vcov. = sandwich::vcovHC(model, type = "HC1"))
}
```

## Retrieving your work

This and all future homework .Rmd files are written in Markdown. The .Rmd file can be rendered as an .html file for easier viewing.

Once you have opened the .Rmd file, you may begin writing your answers beneath each problem. Do not remove any of the original problems from the file, because that makes it more difficult for the me to grade your assignment.

## Submitting your work

When you upload your files to Canvas, you are to submit ***two*** files:

a.  Your reproducible document file (.Rmd) which should be saved as homework##-ID.Rmd. For example, my homework10 file would be saved as homework10-jperrigan.Rmd.

b.  Your rendered reproducible document file (.html) which should be saved as homework##-ID.html. For example, my homework10 file would be saved as homework10-jperrigan.html.

Your ID is your Canvas username. It is also the text before the "@" symbol in your UNO email address.

You have an unlimited number of submissions, but only the latest submission will be viewed and graded. **Proper means that the file is correctly named and formatted. Latest means that the file is the most recent submission prior to the deadline. Remember the .Rmd file needs to render properly to .html before submitting.**

### Use the URLs to access the data. No local files allowed.

This assignment uses the Grunfeld panel: annual observations on investment and capital for 10 firms from 1935 through 1954. You will examine three versions of the investment story:

1. **Across and within firms:** Do observations with more capital also have more investment?
2. **Within a firm over time:** When a firm has more capital than is usual for that firm, does it also invest more than usual?
3. **Across firms in a year:** In a given year, do firms with more capital than other firms also invest more?


## Data and setup

The `Grunfeld` data are included with the `plm` package. The dataset documentation describes the variables and units.

```{r data}
data("Grunfeld", package = "plm")

# The panel index tells plm which firm and year each row represents.
df <- pdata.frame(Grunfeld, index = c("firm", "year"))
```

```{r inspect-data}
dplyr::glimpse(Grunfeld)
```

Before modeling, check what one row represents, which firms and years appear, and how investment and capital are measured. You will need those details to interpret a one-unit change correctly.
